FAQ

Frequently asked questions

Clear answers about eligibility, physical tests, training, fees, appointment and the app's limits.

Is this an official Swedish Police app?

No. RushLabs developed it independently. It does not replace Police training, instructions or decisions.

What are the basic entry requirements?

Applicants must, among other things, be at least 20, hold Swedish 1 or equivalent, complete training and be found suitable.

What physical thresholds are published?

Run 2 kilometres within 12 minutes and lift and drag a 77-kilogram dummy at least 15 metres, or an equivalent load.

How long is basic training?

At least 160 lesson hours over approximately four weeks according to the current Police page.

What are the current fees?

On September 19, 2026, the Police lists SEK 990 to apply and SEK 12,500 including VAT for basic training. Recheck before payment.

How long can appointment last?

Up to five years. A new appointment requires another application and refresher training.

Does the app provide practical competence?

No. Physical techniques, equipment and emergency care require current instructor-led training.

Does the app contain official exam questions?

No. Its 500 questions and explanations are independently authored.

Which Store is available?

The App Store is public for the exact app ID. The Google Play listing is not public as of September 19, 2026.

Is a RushLabs account required?

No. Study records are stored on the device.
